According to reports, Apple is planning to launch a brand-new Home product on October 13, along with a new operating system reportedly named "homeOS." Here are the details.

homeOS will run on a new product called "HomePad," incorporating design elements from other Apple operating systems

Apple's highly anticipated "HomePad" smart home hub is reportedly set to debut on October 13. According to Mark Gurman, the device will run a brand-new operating system reportedly named "homeOS."

A recent Bloomberg report has shed light on several details about homeOS. Its design is reportedly a blend of elements from other Apple operating systems, including:

  • iPhone-style widgets
  • iPad-style app design
  • Apple Watch-style home screen icons

According to Gurman, the default interface "primarily revolves around a photo slideshow and clock display, similar to the upcoming new StandBy mode on the iPhone Duo," with users able to "swipe up from the clock or photo screen to open the app launcher."

Over the past week, we've seen multiple leaks about this Photo Face feature in homeOS, as shown below.

Siri AI will serve as the primary input method, but Apple apps and the home screen will also support touch input

Siri AI will be at the core of homeOS interactions. Gurman stated on his latest podcast:

However, voice won't be the only means of interaction. Apple apps and the home screen will also be part of homeOS. Siri AI can be used to control these apps, while touch input will also be supported.

Built-in apps in homeOS will include Music, Podcasts, Photos, Weather, FaceTime, Notes, Calendar, Messages, Reminders, and more. An App Store is not expected, but third-party widgets can be brought over from your iPhone.

However, just like the existing HomePod, most of the time users will interact with homeOS through Siri.
